<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"a62aefbf9569f298131060e12fb4212e6c83d90fb41e674bdb564f9e12fba34a"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's complaint is a first-party Google Calendar onboarding card ("Welcome to your new Google Calendar" plus "Mobile apps" app-store badges), which is within the AdGuard Annoyances filters' scope, but the reported URL requires a signed-in Google account:⁠ it 302'd through accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin to the workspace.google.com marketing page, and the login-free calendar.google.com embed view — whose complete full-page capture was inspected and shows no such card — is not the reporter's page. Analysis only:⁠ the signed-in view is unreachable in this run, so no selector could be observed or validated.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- No route to reach a reported page that sits behind an account sign-in wall: The reported URL https:⁠//calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/r is served only to a signed-in Google account:⁠ in the locked browser_extension session it returned 302 to accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin and ended on https:⁠//workspace.google.com/intl/en-US/products/calendar/. The public embed view (calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=…holiday…) does load, but the reported "Welcome to your new Google Calendar" onboarding card is not present there, and no tool returns the DOM of the signed-in view. Neither the run instruction nor the linked guidance documents say how to handle a report whose page requires a login (no authenticated profile, no reporter DOM export), nor whether such a report should be handed to a maintainer. A cosmetic rule cannot be written or validated without the element's identifiers, so the run can only report the unreachable flow.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42135665427

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's screenshot is a fake "your file is ready" scam page on a random host, absent from the reported page itself; the article does inject obfuscated ad blocks (div.random) with fake red "Download Game" buttons, and in an unfiltered control one click on such a button opened a tab to gdriveyudu.v40s6146r.space, the same scam-page family. The popup fired only once in \~8 clicks and never in the reporter's own filter profile, so neither the prevent-window-open scriptlet nor hiding div.random could be verified, and both were rejected by the review, which counts the comments-iframe white area as residue.

## Still visible after the rule

- Download Links section, below 'All file hosting links are interchangeable' — Large white rectangular placeholder/frame occupying the area directly below the download-links list. No ad creative or label is visible inside it, but a visible blank ad-wrapper/reserved-space block remains at the reporter-named ad location below the download links.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42142077191

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The daily.dev post page shows a fixed bottom "Open daily.dev app" install banner ("See all posts" + dog mascot, no close button) that covers the lower article; verified that the domain-scoped element-hiding rule daily.dev#⁠#⁠div.fixed:⁠has(a[⁠href*="utm_source=mobile_footer"]⁠) removes it with page integrity intact and nothing else hidden. The rule belongs in the AdGuard Mobile App Banners list (AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt). ## Rule `daily.dev##div.fixed:has(a[href*="utm_source=mobile_footer"])` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile app-install banner (annoyance), not a first-party ad, paywall, German or other anti-adblock wall, or scam page, so no run-instruction policy rule closes it. The repository classifies install-app banners under the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter, whose purpose is exactly 'banners and popups that encourage visitors to install mobile apps'. The filter-policy caveat that footer app banners are decided case-by-case is flagged to the maintainer:⁠ this banner is a fixed overlay covering the lower article with no close control, not an inline footer element. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/15480b24c989b8986e688a9dc3911e6e0cdb82dc/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"ca573a746eea69eb6ee4b881b5b63bfa7fc410100a34dcd493bfe0d0fc7c13a6"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported bottom cookie-consent panel on www⁠.raiffeisen.ru is a first-party `.CookieDialog` element that the repository already targets with `raiffeisen.ru##.CookieDialog` (AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt), so no new rule is warranted. The locked AdGuard CLI environment reported that very rule as applied but injected no element-hiding CSS into the page's main document, so no candidate could be verified and the outcome is analysis-only.

## Still visible after the rule

- Bottom of TILE 1, below 'Как стать клиентом и открыть продукты банка' — Fixed rounded light-gray cookie consent panel overlaying the page; it contains the cookie-processing text and a 'Понятно' button.
- Bottom of viewport, overlaid across the lower page content — Fixed dark rounded cookie-consent panel visible at the bottom of the mobile viewport. It contains the consent text “Продолжая пользоваться сайтом, я соглашаюсь с условиями обработки файлов cookie” and a white “Понятно” button.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42141397342

<sub>Automated analysis against filters at `15480b2`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.</sub>

The list unexpectedly changes from **summary view** to **title-only view**. > 2. The website does not load the actual second page correctly. > 3. ### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.einfomax.co.kr%2Fnews%2FarticleList.html%3Fsc_section_code%3DS1N16%26view_type%3Dsm) ### Comment > ## Title > > Pagination and list view break on `news.einfomax.co.kr` when AdGuard filtering is enabled > > ## Website > > https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm > > Section: Bonds / FX (`채권/외환`) > > ## Environment > > - OS: Windows 11 > - Browser: NAVER Whale > - Ad blocker: AdGuard > - AdGuard filtering: Enabled > - AdGuard version: [please insert version] > > ## Problem > > When AdGuard filtering is enabled, pagination on the article list page of `news.einfomax.co.kr` does not work correctly. > > The issue is especially reproducible in the **summary view**. > > When I open the Bonds / FX article list in summary view and click page `2`: > > 1. The list unexpectedly changes from **summary view** to **title-only view**. > 2. The website does not load the actual second page correctly. > 3. It effectively returns to or remains on the first-page article list. > 4. Further pagination also fails, so I cannot browse page 2, 3, etc. normally. > > The same problem also occurs when using the site's **title-only article list**: with AdGuard enabled, only the first page can be viewed correctly and navigation to later pages does not work. > > ## Steps to reproduce > > 1. Open NAVER Whale. > 2. Enable AdGuard filtering. > 3. Visit: > > https://news.einfomax.co.kr/news/articleList.html?sc_section_code=S1N16&view_type=sm > > 4. Make sure the article list is displayed in **summary view**. > 5. Click page `2` at the bottom of the page. > 6. Observe that: > - the view changes unexpectedly to title-only mode, and/or > - the second page is not loaded correctly, > - pagination stops working normally. > > 7. Disable AdGuard filtering. > 8. Reload the same page and repeat the same steps. > 9. Pagination works normally and the selected list view is preserved. > > ## Expected behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view should remain in summary view. > - Title-only view should remain in title-only view. > - Clicking page `2`, `3`, etc. should load the corresponding article list correctly. > > ## Actual behavior > > With AdGuard enabled: > > - Summary view may unexpectedly change to title-only view. > - Page 2 and later pages do not load correctly. > - The article list effectively remains stuck on page 1. > - Pagination works normally again after AdGuard is disabled. > > ## Additional information > > This appears to be a filtering-related site breakage rather than an issue with the website itself, because the same pagination works correctly when AdGuard is turned off. > > It may be worth checking whether one of the AdGuard filtering rules is blocking a request, script, or parameter used by: > > - pagination > - article list view switching > - page number handling > > ## Screenshots > > - Screenshots 1–2: AdGuard enabled — pagination/list view broken > - Screenshots 3–4: AdGuard disabled — pagination works normally > > Please check for a possible false positive or site compatibility issue in the filtering rules. ### Screenshots

Observe that: > - the view changes unexpectedly to title-only mode, and/or > - the second page is not loaded correctly, > - pagination stops working normally. > > 7. Disable AdGuard filtering. > 8. comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"3e811bef915863da6247e1ab761ec505b2614ac14414270a0a710a356875297a"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — luluvido.com runs a first-party anti-adblock wall inside its player iframe:⁠ showADBOverlay()/showGuardOverlay() injects an obfuscated overlay, keeps it alive with a MutationObserver and destroys the jwplayer, triggered by the first-party just-detect-adblock library /js/jdadbl.js and matching the reporter's screenshot text exactly. The wall never renders in this filtered baseline (__adbDetected = false, no overlay, no difference between phases), so no candidate could be validated; the best unverified rule, carried for human review, is the domain-scoped scriptlet neutralizing the wall entry point.

## Candidate for review

`luluvido.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-property-read', 'showADBOverlay')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: apply_rule returned environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with validationSkipped and errorKind 'baseline_symptom_absent':⁠ the wall is absent in every phase, so the candidate was never judged (2 attempts remained). In the player iframe https:⁠//luluvido.com/e/7gqji6oi42ql justDetectAdblock is defined, __adbDetected is false, no guard overlay exists and no stylesheet hides the bait, so this proxy environment never triggers the detector. A cosmetic hide could not replace it:⁠ the overlay classes are randomised per load (.a899302 then .a793512 on the same URL), it has no CSS display:⁠none (so the sibling family selector in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt:⁠4335 cannot match), the MutationObserver re-shows it, and showGuardOverlay removes the jwplayer. Blocking /js/jdadbl.js was rejected because the page then calls showADBOverlay() immediately.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42153033138

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Arcade Punks serves an English anti-adblock gate ("Ads keep Arcade Punks running" / "AD BLOCKER DETECTED") built \~3 s after load by the page's own inline script, which locks scrolling and hides the page if the modal is hidden — so element hiding cannot work, as the reporter found. A scriptlet that aborts that inline script verified clean in the A/B/C experiment (gate gone, page intact, no residue), so the run proposes it for BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt. ## Rule `arcadepunks.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'document.createElement', 'Network or DNS blocker detected')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page and the gate are English, so the German-wall exclusion does not apply. Not the site's own advertising and not a paywall:⁠ the reported target is an anti-adblock gate injected over already-loaded article content, not an ad and not content access control. The report is an anti-adblock wall whose detector script was captured:⁠ the page's inline wall script was read from the DOM and shows the decoy-offsetHeight and pagead2 probe detection vectors that produce the gate. Filter policy allows blocking anti-adblock walls that aggressively insist on removing the ad blocker or effectively prevent using the website:⁠ the gate covers the full viewport, locks scrolling and hides the whole page if the modal is hidden. Not a scam/phishing page; the rule stops the gate and leaves the page content intact (verified). ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/20a879d17f81622e723e4eacb357a0a9b9406162/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 693](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/20a879d17f81622e723e4eacb357a0a9b9406162/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L693). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The «РЕКЛАМА» creatives the reporter screenshotted (valdai.ru, praga) do not appear on news.sportbox.ru loaded with the reporter's own filter lists:⁠ every AdFox/GPM ad container was empty, no ad-serving request was made, and full-page vision found no ad creative or placeholder. Recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy blocks a rule for this report:⁠ the creatives shown by the reporter (valdai.ru, praga) are advertiser creatives delivered through the site's AdFox/GPM ad inventory, not the site's own self-promotion, and this is not a paywall, not an anti-adblock wall and not a scam/phishing page. The report is closed only because the reporter-defined symptom could not be observed on the loaded page, which the run instruction phrases as 'the report says no rule is needed' and leaves for a maintainer to accept.

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"d7d2f1a7c5b2bb14a6295bff9ff73644d7f96633a93162d789fcc6fe69b69132"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The reported teneriffa-news.com overlay ('Continue reading with ads' / 'Become an Ad-Free Member now') is a Sourcepoint consent/membership gate that renders identically with no ad blocker installed, so it is not an anti-adblock script caused by filtering. Repository policy gives content access measures and German site walls no rule, so I recommend closing without a rule.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

Run instruction:⁠ 'Paywalls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' The reported overlay is the site's own content-access gate - accept ads and continue, or become an ad-free member - not an advertisement or a filtering-induced break. Run instruction:⁠ 'German anti-adblock walls:⁠ no rule; recommend closing.' The site is catalogued as German (its existing rules live in GermanFilter/sections/specific.txt), and even so this wall does not ask the visitor to disable the ad blocker or to allowlist the site; it offers 'Accept and Continue' with ads or a paid membership. Filter policy (AdGuard KnowledgeBase, served via lookup_rule_guidance):⁠ 'Content access measures like paywalls are not blocked by Ad blocking filters', and detection messages are not blocked when they 'provide an alternative to disabling an ad blocker' or 'allow the user to proceed to the website's content'. This overlay does both.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42166426456

An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

comment.body:
@Alex-302 
The key point I’d like to emphasize is that **ads served through Admiral’s proxy are still visible with AdGuard’s default settings**.

In the cases I checked, Admiral used separate domains for displaying its ad wall and serving ads through its proxy. Rather than adding all Admiral-related domains to the Tracking Protection filter, I suggest distinguishing between them based on their purpose and **blocking the proxy domains used to serve ads in AdGuard’s default ad-blocking filters**.

Adblock Plus already blocks these proxy-served ads across a wide range of sites. Could you consider blocking them in AdGuard as well, without requiring users to enable Tracking Protection separately?

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported undismissable goodFOOD registration modal (#⁠zephr-zone-popup) did not appear on the reported Low-Carb Recipes page in either the reporter's filter configuration or a session that resolves the page's consent wall, across reloads, a full scroll and idle waits, while the site's Zephr registration loader was loading normally. No rule is proposed because the element was never observed live, so a selector could not be evidenced or validated; recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules do not cover this report as observed:⁠ the screenshot shows a registration/sign-up prompt ('Join us at the table', 'Create your free account', 'Register now'/'Sign in'), not a first-party ad, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing page, so nothing in the instruction hands it off or blocks a fix. The filter-policy document likewise leaves registration prompts to developer discretion and only forbids circumventing content that asks the user to pay; the observed prompt asks for a free account, so rule generation stays open rather than being policy-blocked. Closing is recommended purely on non-reproduction of the reported target on the successfully loaded reported page, not because a policy rule forbids the rule.

## Artifacts

comment.body:
<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"07b4b2f364ff5a5307656d644c403c5717e490079409f2e726636e70f8ef1a7f"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported İnat TV player gate was reproduced:⁠ a hardcoded "Reklam" Kralbet pre-roll in /event.html withholds the broadcast until the visitor clicks the ad and then "Reklamı geç". A JavaScript rule that triggers the site's own skip path removed the gate and the rotating in-player gambling banners, but the vision review still rejected it for sponsor graphics burned into the video feed, which no filter rule can remove, so no rule could be verified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Video player, top-right corner of the broadcast frame (TILE 1, y=0..1080) — A 'MARSİN SPORTS' gambling sponsor logo with a red 'CANLI' badge is still overlaid on the top-right corner of the playing broadcast, i.e. the gambling ad branding the reporter described as covering the stream persists over the video rather than the stream being clean.
- Video player, strip along the bottom edge of the broadcast frame (TILE 1, y=0..1080) — An overlay banner/ticker strip runs across the lower edge of the player — the red 'SORU VE GÖRÜŞLERİNİZ İÇİN…' line, a white ticker line and a small green sponsor banner logo at the right end — still layered over the broadcast, matching the reporter's 'ad banner across the bottom of the player' symptom.
- Top-right corner inside the video player frame, above the broadcast image — Ad logo/banner overlay reading "MARSİN SPORTS" in red and white sitting directly over the live broadcast in the top-right of the player, the same placement as the gambling logo/banner the reporter described covering the stream.
- Bottom edge inside the video player frame, below the studio image — Full-width banner strip with sponsor/advertising logo and scrolling sponsor text running across the bottom of the player, covering the lower part of the broadcast and sitting where the reporter's bottom bonus banner covers the stream.
- Player top toolbar, right side before the X and share icons — Two small square ad/partner logo tiles displayed in the player header bar alongside the player controls, i.e. advertising creative occupying player chrome above the broadcast.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Missing information

- Scriptlet reference semantics (e.g. trusted-click-element) are not served by the run's guidance documents: The run instruction links only create-own-filters.md, filter-policy.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. lookup_rule_guidance(topic='scriptlet') returns the scriptlet-rule syntax and the trusted-filter restriction, but nothing about individual scriptlet behaviour. I needed to decide between dismissing the site's ad gate with #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '#⁠skip-ad-btn') and a raw #⁠%#⁠ JavaScript rule; whether trusted-click-element clicks an element that is display:⁠none and what its delay/extraMatch parameter order is could not be established from any served document, so that choice had to be made without documented semantics.
- No mapping of rule kinds to the per-filter section files (e.g. which TurkishFilter/sections/*.txt holds #⁠%#⁠ JS rules): CONTRIBUTING.md's placement guidance and the 'AdGuard Turkish filter' section name only the folder (TurkishFilter/sections) and file names for Base/Annoyances, not the section files that hold JavaScript/scriptlet (#⁠%#⁠) rules versus network and element-hiding rules. search_rules exposes filePath values (e.g. SpywareFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt for a scriptlet) but no inventory of existing sections exists for a filter with no JS rules in the queried results, so the exact target file for a #⁠%#⁠ rule in the Turkish filter could not be confirmed from the instruction or the documents.

## Artifacts

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Tumblr's dashboard leaves an empty ad container with an id of the form google_ad_<⁠hex⁠> (min-height 280px) behind because its Google Publisher Tag loader is blocked; the site was observed creating exactly those empty containers on a reachable page. The reported /dashboard URL redirects signed-out visitors to /login, so apply_rule could only report baseline_symptom_absent and the element-hiding candidate stays unverified for human review.

## Candidate for review

`tumblr.com##div[id^="google_ad_"]`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule could not judge it:⁠ https:⁠//www⁠.tumblr.com/dashboard answers 302 and renders /login?redirect_to=%2Fdashboard for a signed-out session, so the filtered baseline page had no element matching div[⁠id^="google_ad_"]⁠ and the experiment ended at baseline_symptom_absent (phases A/B, validationSkipped). The dashboard is behind a login wall this run cannot pass and the login page holds no such container to interact with. The selector is backed by live evidence from /explore/staff-picks, which renders empty div#⁠google_ad_<⁠uuid⁠>.Fuc5D containers with computed min-height:⁠280px while gpt.js is blocked. Unmeasured:⁠ whether hiding the container alone removes the whole dashboard gap.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42182794818

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"b7f367c0a96994cbed933c4b4f66a0fca131651b088750ffce708d91d900ac54"} -->
The filter policy recommends closing without a rule

## Reproduced symptom

The circled regions on intersportv1.live are the site's own betting-affiliate promotion (links to https:⁠//intr.to/NMkbE in its nav, odds widget and footer), with no third-party ad-network request anywhere on the page. Per the run instruction's policy that the site's own advertising gets no rule, the report is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "The site's own advertising (first-party ads):⁠ no rule; recommend closing." The advertising the reporter circled on https:⁠//intersportv1.live/ is rendered by the site's own template as links to its betting affiliate (https:⁠//intr.to/NMkbE) and is served by no third-party ad network, so it is first-party advertising and the policy forbids a deliberate block. Run instruction filter policy:⁠ "Sites with low traffic should still be checked for third-party analytics and advertising networks" - that check was made and found none:⁠ the 87-request HAR of the loaded page contains no ad-server, ad-network, analytics or CMP host, and no element-hiding candidate exists. No rule in the run instruction's policy allows a rule for this case (it is not an anti-adblock wall, not a paywall, not a scam/phishing page), so the report is handed to a maintainer as a closing recommendation rather than a rule.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42181498668

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c3f928ecc50297ad282b2eb7931e572f2053387b2019fa8a03fa845aada90627"} -->
The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The reported anti-adblock gate reproduces host-wide on xn--eckwa2aa3a9c8j8bve9d.gamewith.jp:⁠ the site deletes its own document body and leaves a full-viewport iframe to report.error-report.com/modal?…&⁠error="Cannot find html-load.com script.", so the article is destroyed and no hide or block rule can restore it. Per the run instruction a non-German anti-adblock wall gets a rule only once the captured requests show the detector script, which they do not (no html-load.com/Ad-Shield detector request exists; the detecting code is the site's own), so this is handed to a maintainer — they should review the shared Base-filter Ad-Shield rules before anyone closes it.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ 'Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer.' The captured requests show only gamewith's own error-report endpoints carrying the detection result ('Cannot find html-load.com script.' via error-report.com/report and report.error-report.com/modal); no Ad-Shield detector or recovery script request exists in the capture (html-load.com and recovery.js are never requested) and the detecting code is first-party site code, so the instruction's gate is not met and the report goes to a maintainer. The wall cannot be hidden:⁠ the site removes its own document body and leaves only <⁠head⁠> plus a fixed full-viewport iframe, so element hiding, #⁠$#⁠ or a network block of the wall host each leave an empty page instead of restoring the article. The plausible fixes touch shared, non-project-grouped infrastructure:⁠ gamewith.jp already sits in the shared Base-filter Ad-Shield neutralization rules, and the alternative is scoping or allowlisting html-load.com for the site — shared-rule and vendor-unblocking decisions reserved for maintainers.

## Artifacts

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — tribuntv.online runs a page-authored invisible full-screen overlay that hijacks every click (the player included) into window.open of its promo short link https:⁠//t.ly/fi9RU — the popup the reporter's screenshot shows blocked — and wraps the background and player in the same promo link. The proposed fix, `tribuntv.online#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')` (the repo's established pattern for such streaming sites), could not be verified:⁠ the harness opens no popup in any phase (0 in the baseline too) and the vision review counted the tenant's own background/poster artwork as the unresolved ad.

## Candidate for review

`tribuntv.online#%#//scriptlet('prevent-window-open')`

BaseFilter/sections/general_extensions.txt

Not verified: apply_rule experiment inconclusive; the bound review rejected twice. The symptom is click-triggered:⁠ an inline site script adds a transparent full-viewport overlay (z-index 2147483647) whose click handler calls window.open('https:⁠//t.ly/fi9RU'), and every page click lands on it (interact_page:⁠ click_intercepted for #⁠macth-video and header a; unverifiable_safety for the overlay), so the reported popup cannot be produced. The revealSteps run executed the click in phases A/B/C with popupsOpened 0 in all three - no popup appears in this harness even on the unfiltered baseline. The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Could not reproduce the reported Dailyhunt breakage:⁠ with the reporter's AdGuard filter selection applied, m.dailyhunt.in and two article pages opened from its feed rendered their full content, and the "Something went wrong at our end" error state was absent from DOM text and from structured full-page vision in both the prepared and the CLI evidence session. The applied rules are only ad/tracker blocks that cannot remove article text, so no rule change is warranted; recommend closing as not reproduced.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's filter policy closes first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and non-anti-adblock scams; none of those applies to this incorrect-blocking report, so rule generation is allowed and no policy rule blocks a fix. Because no breakage could be reproduced and no repository rule could be shown to cause it, the recommendation is to close on reproduction grounds, not on policy grounds.

- Issue #⁠246445 lacks the URL of the article page shown in its screenshots: The report's "Issue URL" field is https:⁠//m.dailyhunt.in/ (the Dailyhunt home feed), but both screenshots show an article page about Delhi air pollution / CJI Surya Kant. The article page loaded instead (two m.dailyhunt.in articles reached from the same feed, one by direct navigation and one by client-side navigation from the feed) rendered its full body text with no error state, and structured full-page vision reported the reporter-defined symptom absent. comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Blocking Cookiebot's consent loader (`||consent.cookiebot.eu/uc.js`) leaves mijnpensioen.befrank.nl's Angular login page blank; a domain-pinned exception re-enables it and restores the DigiD/Europees inloggen login card, verified in the A/B/C experiment with no ads returning. ## Rule `@@||consent.cookiebot.eu/uc.js$domain=mijnpensioen.befrank.nl` ## Policy rationale The report is incorrect blocking (legitimate page functionality broken by filtering), not first-party advertising, not a paywall and not a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the instruction's no-rule policy rules applies. The fix restores the blocked consent resource that gates the page's own login card, which is exactly the candidate-rule policy's 'allow the consent mechanism or the blocked resource' case. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_allowlist.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/dcfae04f76718e586912282750d0e67f32e99ce9/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_allowlist.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42192025770 Automated analysis against filters at `dcfae04`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Открываете любой репозиторий в GitHub Codespaces без изменений к белому списку (исключениям HTTPS-фильтрации) -> получаете ошибку подключения, как на скрине №1 (до выключения).

Добавляете домен `tunnels.api.visualstudio.com` или `rel.tunnels.api.visualstudio.com` (второе требует теста) в исключения HTTPS-фильтрации и открываете ту же страницу -> всё загружается корректно, как на скрине №2 ("после выключения")

Наблюдаю жёсткий конфликт между блокировкой рекламы и сохранением прогресса просмотра. > > Сценарий воспроизведения (проверено многократно): > > 1. При включённой фильтрации для «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер»: реклама блокируется, но прогресс просмотра (номер серии и таймкод) не сохраняется. Плеер показывает устаревшую позицию (например, «8 серия» вместо «12»). > 2. При добавлении «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» в исключения фильтрации: прогресс просмотра начинает сохраняться корректно, но реклама возвращается в полном объёме (не редкие проскоки, а полноценные вставки). Редкие микропроскоки длительностью менее секунды, которые наблюдались ранее, объясняются только работой DNS‑фильтрации при отключённой HTTPS‑фильтрации для приложения. > 3. Включение/отключение защиты от трекинга (антитрекинг) в настройках AdGuard не влияет на проблему. > > Предполагаемая причина: служебный запрос для синхронизации позиции просмотра блокируется вместе с рекламой, потому что он идёт через те же домены/эндпоинты. В результате фильтрация либо ломает прогресс, либо (при полном исключении приложения) оставляет рекламу нетронутой. > > Что уже пробовал: > * Отключение антитрекинг‑фильтров — без эффекта. > * Исключение приложения «Я.ТВ Веб-плеер» из фильтрации — прогресс сохраняется, реклама возвращается в полном объёме. > * Анализ поведения при включённом DNS‑фильтре и выключенном HTTPS‑фильтре для плеера — DNS‑фильтрация даёт лишь частичный эффект (редкие микропроскоки), полноценной блокировки рекламы без HTTPS‑фильтрации не получается. > > Прошу помочь: > 1. Подсказать, какой именно запрос (домен/путь/API‑эндпоинт) отвечает за синхронизацию прогресса просмотра в этом сценарии, чтобы можно было добавить точечное исключение и сохранить блокировку рекламы. > 2. Либо добавить в официальные фильтры корректное исключение, которое позволит одновременно блокировать рекламу и не ломать сохранение прогресса. ### Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.malls.ru a floating Yandex ID login prompt panel (div#⁠mya-card, fixed, 352x250px, top-right, z-index 9998) pops up over the article — exactly the element the reporter's arrow marks. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule for that container was verified in the CLI filtering proxy:⁠ the panel was visible on the filtered baseline and gone with the rule, page integrity intact and no layout residue. ## Rule `malls.ru###mya-card` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is a login/registration prompt popup that overlays an article; the AdGuard Popups filter policy explicitly covers registration prompts and other popups that annoy users. It is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules apply. No rule exists in the repository for this selector or widget, so a new rule is needed rather than a shared-family extension. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/37cdcbf892ed60eca4f5a80277b45fd4e57b8c9b/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/popups_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42205397713 Automated analysis against filters at `37cdcbf`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — kazansanatv3.com keeps showing two 1000x90 ad banners (`.reklam-3`, creatives with alt="reklamlar" linking through bit.ly/kznsntvlink and kazn.link/tv). Adding `kazansanatv3.com##.reklam-3` was verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy run:⁠ both banners disappear, the page keeps its layout and its reserved ad height collapses (document 1225px → 1080px). ## Rule `kazansanatv3.com##.reklam-3` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is an advertising problem (label 'T:⁠ Ads', template section 'Issue URL (Ads)'), not a paywall, an anti-adblock wall or a scam page, so none of the closing rules applies. The creatives are advertising content in an explicit ad slot:⁠ the wrapper class is `reklam-3` ('reklam' = ad), the images carry alt="reklamlar" ('ads'), and the banners are click-out creatives routed through a link shortener (bit.ly/kznsntvlink) rather than the site's own product pages; the site's self-promotion (odds widget, nav buttons) links to its own mirror kazn.link and is left visible. Repository precedent:⁠ `betanotv7.site##.reklam-3` (TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt:⁠4790) already hides this same ad-slot class on the twin clone, and the generic `##.reklamalani` (general_elemhide.txt:⁠120) already hides this theme's in-player ad overlay, so maintainers treat these `.reklam*` slots as ad content worth blocking. ## Place in the list [TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/1c6e923b438704751c7ab8c69439c16696c52946/TurkishFilter/sections/specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42212788437 Automated analysis against filters at `1c6e923`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"947a203d4537b2bccec87d044d8aa210d7873672c97eb734c19d86b98685775e"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported cookie notice on www⁠.dukeunctts.com is the Wix website-builder consent banner, and the page's request for its bundle (static.parastorage.com/services/cookie-consent-banner-for-uou/…) is already blocked by the existing shared rule in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt, so no banner element appears and full-page vision finds it absent in both desktop and mobile sessions. Recommend closing:⁠ no new rule is needed because the current Cookie Notices filter already covers this Wix-hosted site.

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy blocks this fix. The report is not about the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not a scam/phishing/tech-support page, so rule generation was permitted. Rule generation was unnecessary on the evidence:⁠ the reporter's cookie notice is the Wix website-builder consent banner, whose loader request the page makes itself, and that request is already blocked on the reported page by the existing shared repository rule ||parastorage.com/services/cookie-consent-banner-for-uou/ in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt (active as AdGuard Cookie Notices filter id 18). No consent-banner element exists in the DOM and full-page vision reports the reporter-defined symptom absent in both the desktop and the mobile session. The run instruction asks the agent never to close an issue itself; this outcome only recommends closing so a maintainer can confirm that the existing shared rule already covers this Wix-hosted site.

## Missing information

- Reporter settings import cannot be applied in the adguard_cli browser model: Issue #⁠246464 carries a reporter settings import URL (product_type=and). The run instruction requires that, when the launch takes `settings`, the reporter profile be `reported_on_current` with that import URL and that only such a session may verify a rule. In the locked adguard_cli environment the evidence session must be launched with extension:⁠"none" (the proxy already filters), and launch_browser rejects any `settings` on a control session ("Expected never but received Object"), so no reported_on_current session was possible. The supplied profile fields also cannot be mapped:⁠ the reporter is AdGuard for Android + Samsung Browser on a mobile device with DNS filtering and Stealth Mode options, none of which the proxy session reproduces. This run therefore used the issue-derived agent_selected profile (desktop 1920 and mobile 375 viewports, en-US, untouched consent) and records the gap rather than claiming reporter parity.

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42216075251

@zloyden Thanks, but why does this fix appear in the AdGuard Other Annoyances filter list? I don't use that list, but I tried enabling it (updated to the latest version) and the empty space block is still there. The blocked element is a carousel that may show ads or self-promotion. The carousel seems to be blocked by the AdGuard Ukrainian and Russian filter lists. Disabling only the Ukrainian filter list makes just the carousel's buttons appear. Disabling both unblocks the whole carousel. Disabling only the Russian filter list changes nothing.
Screenshot with the AdGuard Ukrainian and Russian filter lists disabled
While I'm at it, I want to report that the desktop version of that page shows ad banners. I'm using AdGuard for Windows with the same configuration as in my AdGuard for Android, with the AdGuard Ukrainian and Russian filter lists enabled.
